_metadata.independence: Apart from the brief, I read only x17-re-input.json and no other file, repository content, web page or API.

hints.reason: The instantly familiar saying "as American as apple pie" carries both sides: AMERICA via the idiom, APPLE via apple pie.

pairs.pair_note: Easy but clean; the idiom is about as familiar as U.S. phrases get.

hints.reason: APPLE via the Fuji apple variety and JAPAN via Mount Fuji (and the apple's Japanese origin); a neat double reference.

pairs.pair_note: Text is accurate: it says the apple was developed in Japan without claiming it is named after the mountain (it is named after the town of Fujisaki); keep it that way.

hints.reason: BACK via the film title Back to the Future and TIME via the DeLorean time machine; one iconic reference fits both.

pairs.pair_note: Strong pop-culture hint.

hints.reason: MARIO via the Mario Kart series and BANANA via its signature banana-peel item; both click once Mario Kart comes to mind.

pairs.pair_note: MARIO side is very direct; BANANA is the small payoff.

hints.reason: BEAT via DJs mixing beats and DROP via the dance-track drop (and "drop the beat"); a fair, easy club-music link.

pairs.pair_note: Plain but honest on both sides; no obviously better single word.

hints.reason: PILOT via the Wright brothers' 1903 first flights and BIKE via their well-known bicycle shop; real history with an aha payoff.

pairs.pair_note: The bicycle-shop fact is school-level history for most U.S. players; the indirect route is the kind the owner likes.

hints.reason: Jenga is literally a tower of wooden blocks, so BLOCK and TOWER both come straight to mind.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, satisfying, accurate.

hints.reason: BOLT via Harry Potter's lightning-bolt scar and HOGWARTS via Harry himself; the Hogwarts side is one step indirect but fair.
hints.fix: HOGWARTS: Hogwarts student Harry Potter is famous for his lightning-bolt scar.

pairs.pair_note: The HOGWARTS line's "marks him out as soon as he arrives at Hogwarts" is an embellished scene (he is already famous before Hogwarts); the suggested line keeps it factual.

hints.reason: BOW via Katniss's signature bow and FIRE via her nickname "the girl on fire"; both are core Hunger Games facts.

pairs.pair_note: Good character hint with two genuine attributes.

hints.reason: BROOM via Harry's Nimbus 2000 and CLOUD via nimbus as a rain-cloud word (cumulonimbus); a satisfying double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent pairing; the brand name really does come from the cloud word.

hints.reason: Two different Benjamins: BUTTON via The Curious Case of Benjamin Button and ELECTRICITY via Benjamin Franklin's experiments; a fun shared-name aha.

pairs.pair_note: Franklin is the obvious first thought; finding Button as the partner is the payoff.

hints.reason: CAMP via Everest Base Camp and SUMMIT via the famous push to the top of Everest; both are standard Everest vocabulary.

pairs.pair_note: Accurate and clean.

hints.reason: KING via the royal crown and CAP via a dental crown (commonly called a cap); a clear double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Synonym flag is a note only; both senses are genuine and familiar.

hints.reason: CAT via cats scratching and RECORD via DJ scratching on vinyl; a crisp double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Strong.

hints.reason: SQUARE via the 64 squares of a chessboard and CHECK via putting the king in check during chess; fair, though CHECK belongs to the game more than the board.

pairs.pair_note: Works fine; GINGHAM (a check pattern of squares) would be an alternative double-meaning route, but not clearly better.

hints.reason: HELL via Dante's Inferno and CIRCLE via its nine circles of hell, a widely known cultural phrase.

pairs.pair_note: Classic and accurate.

hints.reason: CLUB via the club sandwich and HERO via the hero sandwich; a category hint with nice misdirection since both words usually mean something else.

pairs.pair_note: HERO for a sub is regional in origin but well known across the U.S.

hints.reason: COMPUTER via silicon chips (Silicon Valley) and SAND via silica, the main component of most sand; true science with an aha.

pairs.pair_note: Text is suitably hedged ("most sand is largely silica").

hints.reason: KID via The Karate Kid title and CRANE via its famous crane kick finale; both are iconic.

pairs.pair_note: Strong.

hints.reason: DANCE via the famous arm-spelling dance to the Village People song and YOUNG via the Y in Young Men's Christian Association; a satisfying two-layer hint.

pairs.pair_note: The YOUNG side is a real aha for many players.

hints.reason: SOLDIER via AWOL as military absence without leave and DESERT via the verb sense (to desert your post), cleverly disguised by the sandy noun on the board.

pairs.pair_note: Text correctly keeps AWOL and desertion as close but not identical.

hints.reason: SWITZERLAND via the Alpine Matterhorn and DISNEY via Disneyland's Matterhorn Bobsleds ride; a fun, true pairing.

pairs.pair_note: The Disney ride is a well-known landmark for U.S. park-goers.

hints.reason: Both DONKEY and PIN arrive through the blindfolded party game Pin the Tail on the Donkey; fair, though a player may think of a pinata first.

pairs.pair_note: TAIL is more direct (a donkey's tail; pin the tail); BLINDFOLD is the more scenic route and still clicks, so both can stand.

hints.reason: DUCK and SEASON via the classic "Duck season!" "Rabbit season!" gag played out in front of hunter Elmer Fudd.

pairs.pair_note: A beloved classic-cartoon bit; text is accurate.

hints.reason: ELECTRICITY via an electrical conductor and TICKET via a train conductor checking tickets; a clean double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Strong.

hints.reason: FAMILY via The Addams Family and HAND via Thing, the family's disembodied hand; the HAND side is the payoff.

pairs.pair_note: Thing is widely known, especially after recent revivals.

hints.reason: A quill is a feather pen dipped in ink, so FEATHER and INK both follow directly.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and accurate.

hints.reason: FINGER via digit as a finger or toe and NUMBER via the digits 0 to 9; a classic double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Strong.

hints.reason: A USB stick is called both a flash drive (FLASH) and a thumb drive (THUMB); a neat everyday aha.

pairs.pair_note: DRIVE would also join both, but USB is less of a phrase-join and more satisfying.

hints.reason: SWORD via Zorro the masked swordsman who slashes a Z, and FOX via zorro being Spanish for fox; true and satisfying.

pairs.pair_note: The Spanish meaning is fairly well known in the U.S. and lands as an aha even for those who did not know it.

hints.reason: Two Starks: GENIUS via Tony Stark's "genius, billionaire, playboy, philanthropist" line and WINTER via House Stark's "Winter Is Coming"; a clever two-franchise link.

pairs.pair_note: Both references are mainstream; strong.

hints.reason: GOLD via the Golden Fleece of Greek myth and RAM via the winged ram it came from (and fleece as sheep's wool); a true and tidy link.

pairs.pair_note: GOLD line ("made of gold wool") is slightly clunky but acceptable; "The Golden Fleece is the golden wool of a magical ram" would read better if editing anyway.

hints.reason: HAIR via a wig being a hairpiece and JUDGE via the traditional British court wig, an image well known to U.S. audiences.

pairs.pair_note: "Traditionally" correctly hedges the British custom.

hints.reason: HERBS and SECRET via Colonel Sanders' famous secret recipe of 11 herbs and spices; a fun brand link.

pairs.pair_note: Lines are hedged as KFC's own claim; good.

hints.reason: HORSE via a breeding stud and LEGO via the studs on top of every brick; a clever double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: The Lego term is familiar to anyone who has built with the bricks; PG in this sense.

hints.reason: JUMP and SHARK via Fonzie's 1977 water-ski shark jump on Happy Days, origin of the phrase "jump the shark".

pairs.pair_note: Older reference, but the phrase keeps it widely known; accurate text.

hints.reason: LAMP via the hopping Luxo Jr. lamp in Pixar's logo and SOUL via the 2020 Pixar film; the SOUL side needs recall of one film among many but is fair.

pairs.pair_note: LAMP is the instant link; SOUL is a solid second once the player scans for Pixar titles.

hints.reason: MAGICIAN via making things vanish and THIN via the idiom "vanish into thin air"; the phrase is instantly familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Phrase-join on the THIN side, but a natural, satisfying one.

hints.reason: MIND via the phrase "Mind the gap" and SUBWAY via the London Underground where it is announced (and the platform gap itself); widely known to U.S. players.

pairs.pair_note: British in origin but one of the best-known British phrases in the U.S.; flag is a familiarity note only.

hints.reason: NORTH via a compass needle and POINT via a needle's sharp point (and the needle that points); fair and clear.

pairs.pair_note: COMPASS (compass points, points north) is a comparable alternative, not clearly better.

hints.reason: PICTURE and SCREEN both via being made of pixels; true but flat, and clearly weaker than BIG ("the big picture", "the big screen").
hints.fix: SCREEN: A digital screen shows images as a grid of pixels.

pairs.pair_note: Accurate but unremarkable; PICTURE and SCREEN are near-synonyms, so the hint barely adds an aha. BIG gives a double idiom. The SCREEN line's "lights up millions of pixels" overgeneralises (not every screen is digital or has millions). Marked uncertain because both connections are honest.

hints.reason: Aretha Franklin's title "Queen of Soul" delivers QUEEN and SOUL together.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, accurate, satisfying.

hints.reason: ROAD and YELLOW via the instantly familiar "yellow brick road" from The Wizard of Oz.

pairs.pair_note: Phrase-join, but the phrase is iconic and the pairing clicks.

hints.reason: SAND via a sand dune and WORM via the giant sandworms of Dune; a neat word-plus-franchise double.

pairs.pair_note: Strong, helped by the recent films.

hints.reason: SHEEP via a shepherd's flock and STAFF via the shepherd's crook; a clear, classic image.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and accurate.

hints.reason: SMELL and SPIRIT via Nirvana's signature song "Smells Like Teen Spirit", with nirvana's spiritual sense as a bonus nudge toward SPIRIT.

pairs.pair_note: A title-join, but the song is iconic and both targets sit in it; satisfying.

hints.reason: WHALE and WHITE via Moby Dick, the famous white whale hunted by Captain Ahab.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, accurate.
